statement0:
The word "memory" is mentioned two or more times in 10.2% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "memory" , 34.5% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This rate is similar to median Psychology paper (shown in black); relative to other words, papers with "memory" are in the top 59th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better).
Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "memory" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (14th percentile among all words) but tend to be cited more (76th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "memory" (14th percentile).
